scenes.heading: Vacuum
scenes.narration: VACUUM permanently deletes old data files that a Delta table no longer references, reclaiming storage.

scenes.heading: Why you need it
scenes.narration: Because Delta writes new files instead of editing in place, updates leave behind obsolete files. Left alone, those files quietly grow your storage bill. VACUUM removes them, while a retention window protects files still needed by in-flight queries and recent time travel.

scenes.heading: Running VACUUM safely
scenes.narration: A DRY RUN first lists the files that would be deleted without touching anything. When you are satisfied, running VACUUM with a retention of one hundred sixty-eight hours removes unreferenced files older than seven days. That retention window is what keeps recent versions available for time travel.

scenes.text: Never set retention below your time-travel needs; vacuuming too aggressively can break the ability to query past versions.
scenes.narration: Never set the retention below your time-travel needs, because vacuuming too aggressively can permanently break your ability to query past versions.
